title: Concise handoff: candidate playback - Tomas Rivera
body:
Quick context:
- Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (serving-runtime) - IC-heavy, some cross-team design.
- Interview loop: phone screen (30m), system-design (60m), pairing exercise (90m), behavioral panel (45m).
- Candidate: Tomas Rivera — ex-startup infra lead, 6+ yrs GPUs + distributed systems, some C++ perf work but primarily Python + CUDA ops surface.

Top-line impression (2-sentence):
Tomas is a thoughtful systems engineer who reasons from performance tradeoffs and can sketch pragmatic rollout paths. He lacks recent owner-level experience in production GPU fleet ops at multi-region scale but has strong signals for being able to get there with targeted onboarding.

Raw notes (verbatim-ish from loop):
- Phone screen: calm, clear framing of past product impact (reduced inference latency by ~30% at previous company via batching+kv-cache changes). Emphasized cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Design: started with high-level constraints, enumerated candidate architectures (sharded KV vs local caching vs prefix routing), sketched fallback behavior. Missed one anti-pattern (locking on KV cache writes under heavy write concurrency) until prompted.
- Pairing (live coding): given a simplified continuous-batching sketch; implemented a naive batcher quickly, then iterated to avoid head-of-line blocking. Struggled briefly with boundary conditions for partial batches and timeouts, but accepted feedback and refactored to a more robust loop.
- Behavioral panel: described an incident where a model rollout caused cost blowup; candidate took responsibility, initiated canary rollback and capacity throttling. Good blameless framing.

Strengths:
- Performance-first mental model: consistently ties choices back to latency/cost/99th-percentile.
- Pragmatic tradeoff analysis: prefers incremental changes with measurement hooks rather than big-bang rewrites.
- Pairing stamina: stayed focused through a long pairing session and responded to critique constructively.

Risks / Concerns:
- Scale experience gap: limited exposure to heterogeneous multi-region GPU pools and autoscaling policies used at our Dedicated product.
- Systems breadth: C++/kernel-level optimization exposure is moderate but not deep — may need senior mentoring to OWN low-level runtime kernels.
- Operational polish: sparse notes on SLO-driven alerting and playbooks; would want to probe runbooks and oncall handling more if we move forward.

Scoring (1-5, 5=strong hire):
- System design (runtime): 4
- Low-level perf/C++ kernel understanding: 3
- Distributed/ops (autoscale, multi-region): 3
- Collaboration/communication: 4
- Ownership/incident handling: 4
- Overall net: 3.5 -> leaning towards hire at Senior (L4) with expectation of ramp plan to L5 in 6-9 months.

Pairing takeaways (actionable):
- Good approach to batching loop, but needs a checklist for edge cases: partial-batch flush heuristics, latency tail handling, abort/backpressure behavior. Recommend adding pairing note to candidate feedback to indicate the areas for early mentoring.
- Suggest exercise in follow-up (optional): give a small perf bug in C++ kernel and ask for triage plan + rollout strategy to observe kernel debugging instincts.

Interview questions to follow up on (if hiring committee wants more signal):
- Walk me through a time you redesigned a cache invalidation strategy that impacted tail latency.
- How have you structured SLOs and alert thresholds for tokenized inference endpoints?
- Concrete example of a kernel-level optimization you shipped (what profiler, delta, risk controls).

Recommendation / next steps:
- Status: hold and discuss calibration with hiring panel. My recommendation: extend an L4 offer with strong expectations written in the ramp plan (kernel pairing, multi-region autoscale exposure, SLO ownership) OR ask for a targeted deep-dive interview focused on kernel/ops if the team wants E2E L5 confidence.

Suggested onboarding guardrails if we hire (notes to hiring manager):
- 90-day plan: 1) pairing on a hot path kernel + perf regression test-suite access; 2) own a small rollout (canary -> target -> ramp) for a cache/prefix optimization; 3) shadow oncall for two rotations.
- Mentorship: pair with a runtime senior (recommended: Ari Chen) for first 3 months.

Misc (notes to self):
- Candidate asked about remote-first culture and relocation stipend — HR to confirm.
- Flag for compensation: current band expectations aligned but asks for clarity on promo path to L5.
- Save this for loop-compare doc and attach to JIRA-ENG-8124.

Raw tags / shorthand used in loop: perf-first, pragmatic, needs-kernel-pairing, ramp-90d

End of scratchpad — convert to a one-page feedback for panel if we move to consensus.
